name: Ir
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog bookkeeping/retired languoid; only Ferlus 1974 wordlist note that Ir is identical to Ong; no phonological description found

sources.citation: Gehrmann, Ryan. 2022. Desegmentalization: towards a common framework for the modeling of tonogenesis and registrogenesis in mainland Southeast Asia with case studies from Austroasiatic. PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. hdl:1842/39113.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Areal generalisation only, sec. 2.2 pp.5-6: in the MSEA sesquisyllable 'The penult, generally referred to as either the presyllable or minor syllable.., is prosodically non-prominent, being derived from the penult of a historical iambic disyllable'; tone/register culminative, one per word. Ta'oiq treated pp.~84-85 (Table 91, register-conditioned coda mutations citing Ferlus 1974a, Diffloth 1989, Gehrmann 2019); no Ong/Ir stress statement.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives record 65220 (Gehrmann & Conver 2015) and CollEx-Persee project page 'ASEMI-Num' (Univ. Cote d'Azur, 2019-2021).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: ASEMI-Num digitised photographs/monographs of the ASEMI fonds, not the journal ASEMI, so Ferlus 1974 is not online there.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid records irrr1240 (Ir, Bookkeeping) and ongg1239 (Ong-Ir); CLDF values: ongg1239Glottolog's fullest description is a phonology or text collection, sole source Ferlus 1974 'La langue ong' (ref 109644).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnologue comment: Ir [irr] is listed as a separate language 'closest to Ong [oog]' but the two are 'parfaitement identique' (Ferlus 1974:113). No descriptive refs attached to irrr1240; ongg1239 has one (Ferlus 1974).

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul (ed.). 2025. Austroasiatic linguistics, in honour of Michel Ferlus (1935-2024). Chiang Mai: Myanmar Center, Faculty of Humanities, Chiang Mai University. 231 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Contents checked: no chapter on Ong or Katuic; 'Ong' occurs only in the Ferlus bibliography entry 1974f (ASEMI 5.1:113-). Nothing on Ir/Ong stress.

sources.citation: Gehrmann, Ryan & Johanna Conver. 2015. Katuic phonological features. Mon-Khmer Studies 44: lv-lxvii.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent = 0). p.lvi: 'Ta'oiq (also called Ong, Ir or Katang), which is typified by a distinctive tense-marked register system that is restructuring final stop consonants'; sec. 5 Minor syllables: restricted onsets, reduced epenthetic vowel; cites the unpublished Conver, Conver & Schmutz 2014 Ta'oiq phoneme inventory.

sources.citation: Gehrmann, Ryan. 2015. Vowel height and register assignment in Katuic. JSEALS 8: 56-70.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.59: 'Ta'oiq (sub-varieties of which are called Ong, Ir and Katang) has a tense-marked register system (tense register: creaky phonation) that is contrastive for all vowels excepting close central vowels'. Diachronic register only.

sources.citation: Schmutz, Jonathan. 2013. The Ta'oi language and people. Mon-Khmer Studies 42: i-xiii.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnonym/glossonym review only: Ir (Yir, In, Zir) and Ong (Tong, Hantong) as Ta'oi subgroups (Schliesinger 2003), Sidwell 2005 'Ong/Ir/Talan' one dialect; Table 3 lists Ong and Ir as 'dialects in need of data'; 'There seems to be at least an ethnographic difference between the Ta'oi and the Ir and Ong' (pp.ix-x). No phonology.

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2005. The Katuic languages: classification, reconstruction and comparative lexicon. LINCOM Studies in Asian Linguistics 58. Munich: LINCOM Europa. 312 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. 3.2 Ta'Oi sub-group (pp.12-14): 'Ong/Ir/Talan' = one language with clear vs creaky register (Ferlus's 'ton glottal'), segmental inventory Table 3.6 from Diffloth/Ferlus ms./Theraphan. 4.3 PK phonological word (p.28, Fig. 4.3): general Katuic template minorsyllable (C1(V1/C2)) + mainsyllable C3(C4)V2(C5); 4.4.2 (pp.31-32): minorsyllable vowel epenthetic/underspecified. scanned a full-text search for stress/accent all of Part 1 for stress/accent/prominence: only 'stressed the lack of' (p.14) and 'stress the following segment' (p.29), both non-prosodic uses. downloaded from the author's…

sources.citation: Huffman, Franklin E. 1971. Field notebook 27 'Analysis: Ir' (informant Sakorn Hongkeo, 'In' /jiir/ [dyiir], Saravane). Franklin E. Huffman Papers, SEAlang Archives.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Re-read p.16 (the only prose page): consonant/final/vowel charts; 'This language is Iir /jiir/ [dyi:r] (Lao In, Thomas and Headley Ir); it is very close to Lao Bru, possibly just a dialect'; glottalized vs plain vowel contrast, homorganic preocclusion before nasals, lax stops in nasal environment, Cr-/Cl- slight aspiration, 'a certain amount of alternation between Crə- and Cər- in presyllables'. Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Conver, Johanna, Mackenzie Conver & Jonathan Schmutz. 2014. Ta'oiq phoneme inventory and word list. Unpublished document (SIL/Payap circle).
